name: Impossibilism
summary: Impossibilism is the Marxist position that capitalism cannot be reformed into socialism and that a working-class party should campaign only for common ownership and democratic control of production, not for a programme of reforms. Its adherents hold that a conscious majority must win political power peacefully and democratically, reject vanguard parties, nationalisation as socialism and Bolshevik state capitalism, and look to a world without money, wages or states.
scope: The anti-reformist Marxist tradition of the Socialist Party of Great Britain, the World Socialist Movement companion parties and the Socialist Party of Canada, in their mature form. De Leonism and its industrial-union strategy have their own entry and are left out; early Canadian inconsistencies (reform demands, anti-Asian views) are treated as superseded by the mature position.

sources.author: David Anthony Perrin
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of the SPGB on reform, war, Russia, collapse theory, democracy, welfare and socialist planning.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The SPGB proposes the 'communistic abolition of buying and selling', no money, and the abolition of the wages system.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Socialism in the SPGB's account abolishes wage labour, commodity production and money.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The SPGB held that no socialist society can be created by a minority and likened Bolshevism to Blanquism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The SPGB refuted collapse theory, holding capitalism recovers from crises and socialism will not arrive by automatic collapse.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The SPGB held that war is an inevitable product of capitalism's economic organisation.

central-planning.rationale: Perrin records that the SPGB first shared Engels's central-planning view, then moved to devolved, polycentric planning; it favours a planned non-market economy but not central rule.

class-collaboration.rationale: Principle 3 states an antagonism of interests between classes that no partnership can remove.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Declaration describes class struggle and the working class as the last class to win freedom; the SPGB bases itself on Marx's theory of social development.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The SPGB holds that common ownership ends the class antagonism, so class struggle does not continue under socialism.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Lawrence says unions can negotiate marginal wage gains and the SPGB backed unions resisting attacks on living standards.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The SPGB held that socialism cannot be built in backward conditions without majority understanding and rejected a transitional stage.

conscription.rationale: SPGB members opposed conscription in the First World War and appeared as objectors at tribunals, and the Socialist Party of Canada joined anti-conscription campaigns.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The SPGB rejected revolutionary defeatism and held the working class has no interest in either side in a capitalist war.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The SPGB held that Soviet nationalised property under a ruling party is state capitalism, not socialism worth defending.

democracy-best.rationale: The SPGB calls political democracy the workers' greatest tool and in 1990 wholeheartedly supported workers' efforts to win democratic rights.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The SPGB rejected Lenin's dictatorship as party rule over workers and peasants and held that no transitional society stands between capitalism and socialism.

direct-action.rationale: The SPGB holds that political organisation and action are of prime importance and that the capitalist class rests on political power, so it rejects direct action in place of elections.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Declaration says emancipation is without distinction of race, and the commentary calls racial hatreds products of capitalism's insecurity.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialism is described as free access to goods and services, a society geared to meeting human needs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration says working-class emancipation involves all mankind without distinction of race or sex, and the commentary says all are equal in humanity.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Declaration and commentary treat divisions of race and nationality as hatreds bred by capitalism to be removed.

gradual-change.rationale: The SPGB holds that reform steps leave capitalism's basis untouched and works only for the immediate establishment of socialism.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The SPGB bases itself on Marx's labour theory of value and holds that profit is the difference between workers' pay and the value they produce.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Perrin says the SPGB held a firmly materialist basis and Marx's theory of social development, and its Russia analysis rested on it.

means-match-ends.rationale: The SPGB holds that a democratic socialist society needs democratic, majority-based means, which is why it rejects vanguard and violent minority methods.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: The SPGB held that violent revolution by minorities means dead workers and rejected Blanquist conspiratorial organisation.

military-superiority.rationale: The SPGB held capitalist states' arms and war preparations serve ruling-class interests and opposed their wars.

nation-first.rationale: The SPGB calls belief in 'national interests' a poisoning illusion of class harmony and speaks across frontiers to the working class of the world.

national-self-determination.rationale: In 1939 the SPGB stated that the doctrine of self-determination cannot bring peace within capitalism, and it criticised treating the nation as a homogeneous entity.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The SPGB held that socialism and communism are the same system and that a 'transitional society' is nonsensical.

one-party-rule.rationale: The SPGB condemned Bolshevik one-party dictatorship over the working class and holds socialism needs a majority's democratic agreement; no parties exist in a classless society.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Principle 6 calls on the working class to conquer the powers of government through political action, and the commentary calls political democracy the workers' greatest tool.

party-controls-media.rationale: The SPGB criticised Lenin's proletarian dictatorship with press censorship and a ban on other parties.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The SPGB calls belief in 'national interests' a dangerous illusion and a patriot appeal a tool of the capitalist class.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The commentary says the means of production are common but personal belongings such as clothing are not included.

production-for-use.rationale: The Object and the commentary set production for human need against decisions made for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Declaration says workers' labour alone produces wealth, and profit is the gap between wages and the value produced.

public-ownership.rationale: The SPGB says nationalisation was adopted by capitalism and is state ownership by the capitalist class, not common ownership, yet it does not oppose it as a reform.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: In 1911 the Socialist Standard condemned advocacy of excluding Asian fellow-workers from British Columbia, and the Canadian party later looked on all workers equally.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration includes all mankind without distinction of race, and the SPGB treats all workers equally irrespective of origin.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration includes all mankind without distinction of race, and the SPGB condemned racial exclusion of workers.

religion-illusion.rationale: The SPGB's Socialism and Religion holds religion is a reflex of social life that fades with science and ends under socialism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Principle 6 has the working class conquer the machinery of government and convert it into the agent of emancipation, which is taking it over, not smashing it.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: The Declaration says 'revolutionary' war will not be required once a majority supports socialism, and violent revolution never liberated workers.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Principle 5 states that emancipation must be the work of the working class itself.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The commentary says socialism is not a cooperative island in capitalism but a global system, and Russian isolation made socialism there impossible.

socialized-markets.rationale: The SPGB holds socialism has no markets, buying or selling, whoever owns the businesses.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The SPGB's analysis, built on its Russia chapter, judged Soviet Russia state capitalism under a party dictatorship.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Principle 6 says the machinery of government exists only to conserve the capitalist monopoly of wealth.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The SPGB criticised the banning of other parties and censorship in Bolshevik rule; in 1990 it supported democratic rights and freedom of expression.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The SPGB saw imperial expansion as a capitalist rivalry in which workers have no stake.

unions-good.rationale: The SPGB supports efforts of unions to resist attacks on living standards and encourages workers to fight back, while saying unions cannot end capitalism.

vanguard-party.rationale: Principle 1 excludes political leadership, and the SPGB treated Leninist vanguardism as a denial of working-class self-emancipation.

war-builds-character.rationale: The SPGB opposed capitalist wars as against workers' interests, mocking appeals to manhood and honour that bring broken health and graves.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Declaration refuses distinction of sex, and the Canadian party, though anti-reformist, did not oppose votes for women.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Principle 7 requires hostility to all other parties and the SPGB rejected alliances with other class parties.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Principle 7 requires the party to be hostile to every other party, whether labour or capitalist.

workers-nation.rationale: The SPGB calls socialism a global system, says capitalism must be replaced globally and rejects national interests as an illusion of class harmony.

workers-own-party.rationale: Principle 7 commits the party of working-class emancipation to be hostile to every other party.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: The SPGB 'does not support the idea of reforming capitalism and therefore does not work for reforms', and the WSM says a socialist party should not advocate reforms, though it does not oppose reforms that help workers.

notes: The workers-parties-campaign-reforms statement already in the bank captures the defining anti-reform position, so no missing statement is proposed. Strands: Lawrence's 1978 article claims stronger futility for reforms than the 2021 WSM text, which accepts gains from healthcare, education and unions; the answers follow the common core. De Leonist industrial unionism, Bolshevik sympathy and early Canadian reform demands differ and are excluded. Searched themes: reform, war, Russia, democracy, planning, unions, race, religion, nationalism; economy, liberty, ecology, technology and culture statements have no recorded position.
